note: Pressure gauges that events feed and that feed back into the world. Levels run from 0 to 100. Every per-point effect is in log-odds (approval and group approval) and is a calibration choice, not a measured figure.

meters.label: Red Scare
meters.description: Fear of Communist subversion at home: spy trials, loyalty oaths, blacklists and congressional hunts. It makes defence bills easier to pass and the President harder to love, and it bears down on intellectuals and the left.
meters.note: Starts at 12: HUAC's Hollywood hearings (1947), the Hiss case and the Smith Act trial of Communist leaders (from January 1949) were under way, but the scare had not yet peaked. Fades by 6% a quarter unless fed; while McCarthy is unchecked it rises 2 points a quarter (1 once he has been confronted). At 50 it costs the President about 0.15 log-odds (three or four points of approval).

meters.label: War weariness
meters.description: The public's tiring of a war with no end in sight: casualty lists, the draft, controls. It rises every quarter American troops are fighting and fades once they come home.
meters.note: Rises 4 points a quarter while American troops fight in Korea and fades by 10% a quarter, so it settles near 40 in a long war, costing about 0.3 log-odds (six or seven points of approval). Mueller (War, Presidents and Public Opinion, 1973) found support for Korea and Vietnam fell with the logarithm of casualties; this is a simpler stand-in until military units and casualties exist.
